steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
I'll start by exploring the workspace structure to understand what we're working with.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# GRPO | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | FSDP + vLLM, one GPU | GSM8K
3	# verls GSM8K GRPO quickstart scaled to a single GPU. Reward: verls built-in GSM8K
4	# rule (last "#### N" must equal the gold answer), scored by the DAPO reward manager
5	# with the overlong penalty disabled.
6	set -xeuo pipefail
7	
8	W=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
9	cd "$W"
10	
11	MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-$W/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
12	TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k/train.parquet}
13	VAL_FILE=${VAL_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k/test.parquet}
14	LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$W/outputs/run}
15	NGPUS_PER_NODE=${NGPUS_PER_NODE:-1}
16	TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-100}
17	TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-10}
18	SEED=${SEED:-42}
19	
20	TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE=128         # prompts per step
21	ROLLOUT_N=8                  # responses per prompt (GRPO group size)
22	PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE=32       # 4 optimizer steps per training step
23	MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH=512
24	MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512
25	ACTOR_LR=2e-6
26	KL_LOSS_COEF=0.001
27	ROLLOUT_TOP_P=0.5            # nucleus sampling; at temperature 1.0 a 0.5B model otherwise samples stray tokens
28	
29	PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-grpo_gsm8k}
30	EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-qwen2_5_0_5b_gsm8k_grpo}
31	
32	if [ ! -f "$MODEL_PATH/config.json" ]; then
33	    echo "model not found at $MODEL_PATH" >&2; exit 1
34	fi
35	if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_FILE" ] || [ ! -f "$VAL_FILE" ]; then
36	    python3 examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py --local_dataset_path "$W/data/raw/gsm8k" --local_save_dir "$(dirname "$TRAIN_FILE")"
37	fi
38	
39	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
40	export PYTHONPATH="$W${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
41	export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
42	export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
43	export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH="$LOG_DIR/metrics.jsonl"
44	export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
45	
46	DATA=(
47	    algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo
48	    algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False
49	    data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILE"
50	    data.val_files="$VAL_FILE"
51	    data.train_batch_size=$TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE
52	    data.max_prompt_length=$MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH
53	    data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH
54	    data.filter_overlong_prompts=True
55	    data.truncation=error
56	    data.seed=$SEED
57	    data.dataloader_num_workers=0
58	)
59	MODEL=(
60	    actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL_PATH"
61	    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True
62	    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True
63	)
64	ACTOR=(
65	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$ACTOR_LR
66	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE
67	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True
68	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
69	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True
70	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=$KL_LOSS_COEF
71	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl
72	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0
73	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean
74	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.data_loader_seed=$SEED
75	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False
76	    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False
77	)
78	ROLLOUT=(
79	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm
80	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1
81	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4
82	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$ROLLOUT_N
83	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0
84	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=$ROLLOUT_TOP_P
85	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_k=-1
86	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=$SEED
87	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers=1
88	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
89	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
90	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1
91	    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False
92	    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
93	    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
94	)
95	REWARD=(
96	    reward.reward_manager.name=dapo
97	    reward.num_workers=1
98	    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.enable=False
99	    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.len=128
100	    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.penalty_factor=1.0
101	    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.log=False
102	    +reward.reward_kwargs.max_resp_len=$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH
103	)
104	TRAINER=(
105	    trainer.use_v1=False
106	    trainer.critic_warmup=0
107	    trainer.logger=[console,wandb,file]
108	    trainer.project_name=$PROJECT_NAME
109	    trainer.experiment_name=$EXPERIMENT_NAME
110	    trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPUS_PER_NODE
111	    trainer.nnodes=1
112	    trainer.save_freq=-1
113	    trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ
114	    trainer.val_before_train=True
115	    trainer.total_epochs=15
116	    trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS
117	    trainer.resume_mode=disable
118	    trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts"
119	    trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations"
120	)
121	
122	# One GPU, a few CPUs: Ray must not size itself from the whole host.
123	RAY=(
124	    ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=4
125	    +ray_kwargs.ray_init.object_store_memory=6000000000
126	)
127	
128	python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
129	    "${DATA[@]}" "${MODEL[@]}" "${ACTOR[@]}" "${ROLLOUT[@]}" "${REWARD[@]}" "${TRAINER[@]}" "${RAY[@]}" "$@" \
130	    2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"
131

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GRPO | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | FSDP + vLLM, one GPU | GSM8K
# verls GSM8K GRPO quickstart scaled to a single GPU. Reward: verls built-in GSM8K
# rule (last "#### N" must equal the gold answer), scored by the DAPO reward manager
# with the overlong penalty disabled.
set -xeuo pipefail

W=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$W"

MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-$W/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k/train.parquet}
VAL_FILE=${VAL_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k/test.parquet}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$W/outputs/run}
NGPUS_PER_NODE=${NGPUS_PER_NODE:-1}
TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-100}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-10}
SEED=${SEED:-42}

TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE=128         # prompts per step
ROLLOUT_N=8                  # responses per prompt (GRPO group size)
PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE=32       # 4 optimizer steps per training step
MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH=512
MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512
ACTOR_LR=2e-6
KL_LOSS_COEF=0.001
ROLLOUT_TOP_P=0.5            # nucleus sampling; at temperature 1.0 a 0.5B model otherwise samples stray tokens

PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-grpo_gsm8k}
EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-qwen2_5_0_5b_gsm8k_grpo}

if [ ! -f "$MODEL_PATH/config.json" ]; then
    echo "model not found at $MODEL_PATH" >&2; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_FILE" ] || [ ! -f "$VAL_FILE" ]; then
    python3 examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py --local_dataset_path "$W/data/raw/gsm8k" --local_save_dir "$(dirname "$TRAIN_FILE")"
fi

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$W${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH="$LOG_DIR/metrics.jsonl"
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false

DATA=(
    algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo
    algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False
    data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILE"
    data.val_files="$VAL_FILE"
    data.train_batch_size=$TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE
    data.max_prompt_length=$MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH
    data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH
    data.filter_overlong_prompts=True
    data.truncation=error
    data.seed=$SEED
    data.dataloader_num_workers=0
)
MODEL=(
    actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL_PATH"
    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True
    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True
)
ACTOR=(
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$ACTOR_LR
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=$KL_LOSS_COEF
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.data_loader_seed=$SEED
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False
)
ROLLOUT=(
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$ROLLOUT_N
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=$ROLLOUT_TOP_P
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_k=-1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=$SEED
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
)
REWARD=(
    reward.reward_manager.name=dapo
    reward.num_workers=1
    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.enable=False
    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.len=128
    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.penalty_factor=1.0
    +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.log=False
    +reward.reward_kwargs.max_resp_len=$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH
)
TRAINER=(
    trainer.use_v1=False
    trainer.critic_warmup=0
    trainer.logger=[console,wandb,file]
    trainer.project_name=$PROJECT_NAME
    trainer.experiment_name=$EXPERIMENT_NAME
    trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPUS_PER_NODE
    trainer.nnodes=1
    trainer.save_freq=-1
    trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ
    trainer.val_before_train=True
    trainer.total_epochs=15
    trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS
    trainer.resume_mode=disable
    trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts"
    trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations"
)

# One GPU, a few CPUs: Ray must not size itself from the whole host.
RAY=(
    ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=4
    +ray_kwargs.ray_init.object_store_memory=6000000000
)

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
    "${DATA[@]}" "${MODEL[@]}" "${ACTOR[@]}" "${ROLLOUT[@]}" "${REWARD[@]}" "${TRAINER[@]}" "${RAY[@]}" "$@" \
    2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

20	2. Model update staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)

23	Its core capabilities include computing importance sampling (IS) weights,
24	filtering outlier samples via rejection sampling (RS), and
25	tracking metrics to diagnose and correct off-policy issues.

376

378	        combined_mask = combined_mask * token_keep_mask
379	        seq_keep_bool_tensor = (~((~token_keep_bool) & response_mask_bool)).all(dim=-1)
380	
381	        option_metrics = compute_rs_metrics(
382	            option_name=option_name,
383	            rs_statistic=per_token_stat,
384	            response_mask=response_mask,
385	            seq_valid_mask=seq_valid_mask,
386	            level=level,
387	            per_sequence_values=per_sequence_stat,
388	            rollout_rs_threshold=metrics_upper_threshold,
389	            rollout_rs_threshold_lower=metrics_lower_threshold,
390	            apply_lower_threshold=apply_lower_threshold,
391	        )
392	        metrics.update(option_metrics)
393	
394	        token_masked_fraction = verl_F.masked_mean(1 - token_keep_mask, response_mask).item()
395	        seq_valid_float = seq_valid_mask.float()
396	        if seq_valid_float.sum() > 0:
397	            seq_keep_float = seq_keep_bool_tensor.to(dtype=log_ratio.dtype)
398	            seq_masked_fraction = (((1.0 - seq_keep_float) * seq_valid_float).sum() / seq_valid_float.sum()).item()
399	        else:
400	            seq_masked_fraction = 0.0
401	        metrics[f"rollout_rs_{option_name}_masked_fraction"] = token_masked_fraction
402	        metrics[f"rollout_rs_{option_name}_seq_masked_fraction"] = seq_masked_fraction
403	
404	    final_mask = combined_mask
405	    metrics["rollout_rs_masked_fraction"] = verl_F.masked_mean(1 - final_mask, response_mask).item()
406	    final_keep_bool = (final_mask > 0.5) & response_mask_bool
407	    seq_has_masked: torch.Tensor = (~final_keep_bool & response_mask_bool).any(dim=-1)
408	    metrics["rollout_rs_seq_masked_fraction"] = seq_has_masked.float().mean().item()
409	
410	    modified_response_mask: torch.Tensor = (response_mask * final_mask).to(dtype=response_mask.dtype)
411	    return modified_response_mask, metrics

414	def compute_rs_metrics(
415	    option_name: str,
416	    rs_statistic: torch.Tensor,
417	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
418	    seq_valid_mask: torch.Tensor,
419	    *,
420	    level: str,
421	    per_sequence_values: Optional[torch.Tensor],
422	    rollout_rs_threshold: float,
423	    rollout_rs_threshold_lower: float,
424	    apply_lower_threshold: bool,
425	) -> dict[str, float]:
426	    """Compute metrics for hard trust region enforcement (per-option).
427	
428	    Args:
429	        option_name: Original option string supplied by the user.
430	        rs_statistic: Trust region statistic (per token) used for thresholding.
431	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding).
432	        seq_valid_mask: Boolean mask indicating sequences with at least one valid token.
433	        level: "token" or "sequence" describing aggregation level.
434	        per_sequence_values: Optional per-sequence statistic (same semantics as rs_statistic).
435	        rollout_rs_threshold: Upper threshold.
436	        rollout_rs_threshold_lower: Lower threshold (ignored if ``apply_lower_threshold`` is False).
437	        apply_lower_threshold: Whether to mask/log metrics for values below the lower threshold.
438	    """
439	    if not response_mask.any():
440	        raise ValueError("response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).")
441	
442	    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
443	    prefix = f"rollout_rs_{option_name}"
444	    mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()
445	
446	    # Compute sequence statistics (used by several metrics).
447	    if per_sequence_values is not None:
448	        seq_values = per_sequence_values
449	    else:
450	        seq_values = verl_F.masked_mean(rs_statistic, response_mask, axis=-1)
451	    if seq_values.dim() > 1:
452	        seq_values = seq_values.squeeze(-1)
453	    seq_values_valid = seq_values[seq_valid_mask]
454	
455	    # Mean of the statistic (always reported).
456	    metrics[f"{prefix}_mean"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rs_statistic, response_mask).item()
457	
458	    # Max/min values.
459	    if level == "sequence" and seq_values_valid.numel() > 0:
460	        metrics[f"{prefix}_max"] = seq_values_valid.max().item()
461	        metrics[f"{prefix}_min"] = seq_values_valid.min().item()
462	    else:
463	        metrics[f"{prefix}_max"] = rs_statistic.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("-inf")).max().item()
464	        metrics[f"{prefix}_min"] = rs_statistic.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("inf")).min().item()
465	
466	    # Fractions above/below the thresholds.
467	    if level == "sequence" and seq_values_valid.numel() > 0:
468	        fraction_high = (seq_values_valid > rollout_rs_threshold).float().mean().item()
469	        fraction_low = (
470	            (seq_values_valid < rollout_rs_threshold_lower).float().mean().item() if apply_lower_threshold else 0.0
471	        )
472	    else:
473	        fraction_high = verl_F.masked_mean((rs_statistic > rollout_rs_threshold).float(), response_mask).item()
474	        fraction_low = (
475	            verl_F.masked_mean((rs_statistic < rollout_rs_threshold_lower).float(), response_mask).item()
476	            if apply_lower_threshold
477	            else 0.0
478	        )
479	    metrics[f"{prefix}_fraction_high"] = fraction_high
480	    metrics[f"{prefix}_fraction_low"] = fraction_low
481	
482	    # Standard deviation (clamped for stability).
483	    mask_count: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum()
484	    if mask_count > 1:
485	        if apply_lower_threshold:
486	            clamp_min = rollout_rs_threshold_lower
487	        else:
488	            clamp_min = 0.0
489	        stat_for_std: torch.Tensor = rs_statistic.clamp(min=clamp_min, max=rollout_rs_threshold)
490	        mean_clamped: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(stat_for_std, response_mask)
491	        stat_var: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(stat_for_std.square(), response_mask) - mean_clamped.square()
492	        metrics[f"{prefix}_std"] = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(stat_var, min=0.0)).item()
493	    else:
494	        metrics[f"{prefix}_std"] = 0.0
495	
496	    # Sequence-level summary metrics.
497	    if seq_values_valid.numel() > 0:
498	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_mean"] = seq_values_valid.mean().item()
499	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_std"] = seq_values_valid.std().item() if seq_values_valid.numel() > 1 else 0.0
500	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max"] = seq_values_valid.max().item()
501	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_min"] = seq_values_valid.min().item()
502	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max_deviation"] = (seq_values_valid - 0.0).abs().max().item()
503	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_high"] = (seq_values_valid > rollout_rs_threshold).float().mean().item()
504	        if apply_lower_threshold:
505	            metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_low"] = (
506	                (seq_values_valid < rollout_rs_threshold_lower).float().mean().item()
507	            )
508	    else:
509	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_mean"] = 0.0
510	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_std"] = 0.0
511	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max"] = 0.0
512	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_min"] = 0.0
513	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max_deviation"] = 0.0
514	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_high"] = 0.0
515	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_low"] = 0.0
516	
517	    return metrics

520	def compute_rollout_correction_weights(
521	    log_ratio: torch.Tensor,
522	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
523	    rollout_is: str = "token",
524	    rollout_is_threshold: str | float = 2.0,
525	    rollout_is_batch_normalize: bool = False,
526	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
527	    """Compute importance sampling weights to correct for off-policy distribution shifts.
528	
529	    This function calculates IS weights (π_train / π_rollout) using log ratios for numerical stability.
530	    It supports multiple aggregation levels and truncates extreme weights to prevent training instability.
531	
532	    Key design:
533	    - Log-space computations to avoid overflow
534	    - Truncation of extreme weights (TIS: Truncated Importance Sampling)
535	    - Optional batch normalization (normalize to mean=1.0)
536	    - Metrics tracking for weight distribution analysis
537	
538	    Args:
539	        log_ratio: Log ratio of training policy probability to rollout policy probability,
540	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
541	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
542	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
543	        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level, must be one of:
544	            - "token": Per-token weights (biased, low variance)
545	            - "sequence": Per-sequence weight (product of tokens; unbiased, high variance)
546	        rollout_is_threshold: Threshold specification for IS weights.
547	            - Single float or float-like string: TIS, clamp weights to the upper bound
548	            - "lower_upper" string: IcePop, zero weights outside [lower, upper]
549	        rollout_is_batch_normalize: Whether to normalize IS weights to have mean=1.0 per batch,
550	            default False.
551	
552	    Returns:
553	        Tuple containing:
554	            rollout_is_weights: Truncated IS weights (masked to zero for padding tokens),
555	                shape (batch_size, seq_length). If batch_normalize=True, normalized to mean=1.0.
556	            metrics: Dictionary of IS weight metrics (all scalars), including:
557	                - rollout_is_mean/max/min: Statistic of weights (before batch normalization)
558	                - rollout_is_eff_sample_size: Effective sample size (ESS)
559	                - rollout_is_seq_*: Sequence-level weight statistics
560	                - rollout_is_batch_norm_factor: Normalization factor (only if batch_normalize=True)
561	    """
562	    # Validate input parameters
563	    valid_is_levels = {"token", "sequence"}
564	    if rollout_is not in valid_is_levels:
565	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid rollout_is: {rollout_is}. Must be one of {valid_is_levels}.")
566	    rollout_is_threshold_upper, rollout_is_threshold_lower = _parse_rollout_is_threshold(rollout_is_threshold)
567	    use_icepop = rollout_is_threshold_lower is not None
568	
569	    # Compute IS weights from log ratio (handles different aggregation levels)
570	    if rollout_is == "token":
571	        # Per-token IS weight: exp(log(π_train/π_rollout)) with safety clamp
572	        log_ratio_for_metrics: torch.Tensor = log_ratio
573	        log_ratio_safe: torch.Tensor = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
574	        raw_rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe)
575	
576	    elif rollout_is == "sequence":
577	        # Sequence-level IS weight: product of token ratios (exp(sum(log ratios)))
578	        log_ratio_sum: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_sum(log_ratio, response_mask, axis=-1).unsqueeze(
579	            -1
580	        )  # Shape: (batch_size, 1)
581	        log_ratio_for_metrics = log_ratio_sum
582	
583	        log_ratio_sum_safe: torch.Tensor = torch.clamp(log_ratio_sum, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
584	        raw_rollout_is_weights = torch.exp(log_ratio_sum_safe).expand_as(log_ratio)  # Broadcast to sequence length
585	
586	    else:
587	        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_is: {rollout_is}")
588	
589	    # Zero out weights for padding tokens using response mask
590	    raw_rollout_is_weights = raw_rollout_is_weights * response_mask
591	
592	    # Apply TIS for a single upper bound and IcePop for a lower_upper string.
593	    if not use_icepop:
594	        rollout_is_weights = raw_rollout_is_weights.clamp(max=rollout_is_threshold_upper)
595	    else:
596	        assert rollout_is_threshold_lower is not None
597	        token_kept_mask = (raw_rollout_is_weights >= rollout_is_threshold_lower) & (
598	            raw_rollout_is_weights <= rollout_is_threshold_upper
599	        )
600	        rollout_is_weights = torch.where(
601	            token_kept_mask, raw_rollout_is_weights, torch.zeros_like(raw_rollout_is_weights)
602	        )
603	
604	    # Compute IS weight metrics.
605	    metrics: dict[str, float] = compute_is_metrics(
606	        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
607	        raw_rollout_is_weights=raw_rollout_is_weights,
608	        log_ratio_for_metrics=log_ratio_for_metrics,
609	        response_mask=response_mask,
610	        rollout_is=rollout_is,
611	        rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold_upper,
612	        rollout_is_threshold_lower=rollout_is_threshold_lower,
613	    )
614	    if use_icepop:
615	        assert rollout_is_threshold_lower is not None
616	        oob_mask = (raw_rollout_is_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower) | (
617	            raw_rollout_is_weights > rollout_is_threshold_upper
618	        )
619	        metrics["rollout_is_oob_ratio"] = verl_F.masked_mean(oob_mask.float(), response_mask).item()
620	
621	    # Detach weights to prevent gradient flow (mathematically required by IS theory)
622	    # IS weights change the measure, not the objective. See §3.2.2 in docs/algo/rollout_corr_math.md
623	    rollout_is_weights = rollout_is_weights.detach()
624	
625	    # Apply batch normalization if requested
626	    if rollout_is_batch_normalize:
627	        # Compute mean based on aggregation level
628	        mask_float = response_mask.to(dtype=rollout_is_weights.dtype)
629	        if rollout_is == "token":
630	            # Token-level: normalize over all token weights
631	            if torch.distributed.is_available() and torch.distributed.is_initialized():
632	                weights_mean = verl_F.distributed_masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, mask_float)
633	            else:
634	                weights_mean = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask)
635	        elif rollout_is == "sequence":
636	            # Sequence-level: normalize over sequence weights (one weight per sequence)
637	            # For each sequence, compute mean over valid tokens (they all have the same weight)
638	            # then average across sequences
639	            seq_weights = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)
640	            seq_mask = (response_mask.sum(dim=-1) > 0).to(dtype=rollout_is_weights.dtype)
641	            if torch.distributed.is_available() and torch.distributed.is_initialized():
642	                weights_mean = verl_F.distributed_masked_mean(seq_weights, seq_mask)
643	            else:
644	                weights_mean = (seq_weights * seq_mask).sum() / seq_mask.sum().clamp_min(1e-8)
645	        else:
646	            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_is: {rollout_is}")
647	
648	        # Normalize to mean=1.0 (avoid division by zero)
649	        if weights_mean > 1e-8:
650	            rollout_is_weights = rollout_is_weights / weights_mean
651	            metrics["rollout_is_batch_norm_factor"] = weights_mean.item()
652	        else:
653	            metrics["rollout_is_batch_norm_factor"] = 1.0
654	
655	    return rollout_is_weights, metrics
656

658	def compute_is_metrics(
659	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor,
660	    raw_rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor,
661	    log_ratio_for_metrics: torch.Tensor,
662	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
663	    rollout_is: str,
664	    rollout_is_threshold: float,
665	    rollout_is_threshold_lower: Optional[float] = None,
666	) -> dict[str, float]:
667	    """Compute comprehensive metrics for truncated importance sampling weights.
668	
669	    This function calculates statistics for the applied IS weights while using the
670	    raw pre-processing weights to diagnose how often ratios exceed the configured bounds.
671	
672	    Args:
673	        rollout_is_weights: Truncated IS weights (π_train / π_rollout),
674	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
675	        raw_rollout_is_weights: Raw masked IS weights before TIS / IcePop processing,
676	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
677	        log_ratio_for_metrics: Log ratio of training to rollout probabilities (unclamped),
678	            shape varies by aggregation level.
679	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
680	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
681	        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level (matches compute_rollout_correction_weights).
682	        rollout_is_threshold: Upper threshold for truncated IS weights.
683	
684	    Returns:
685	        Dictionary of IS weight metrics (all scalars).
686	    """
687	    if not response_mask.any():
688	        raise ValueError("response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).")
689	
690	    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
691	    device: torch.device = rollout_is_weights.device
692	    # Default lower threshold (reciprocal of upper threshold)
693	    rollout_is_threshold_lower = (
694	        1.0 / rollout_is_threshold if rollout_is_threshold_lower is None else rollout_is_threshold_lower
695	    )
696	
697	    # Precompute log thresholds for accurate checks
698	    log_threshold_upper: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold, device=device))
699	    log_threshold_lower: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold_lower, device=device))
700	
701	    # Compute metrics based on aggregation level
702	    if rollout_is == "sequence":
703	        # Sequence-level aggregation: use log-space for unclamped stats
704	        log_max: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.max()
705	        log_min: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.min()
706	        metrics["rollout_is_max"] = torch.exp(torch.clamp(log_max, max=SAFETY_BOUND)).item()
707	        metrics["rollout_is_min"] = torch.exp(log_min).item()
708	
709	        # Mean uses truncated weights to avoid overflow
710	        metrics["rollout_is_mean"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()
711	
712	        # Fraction of weights exceeding thresholds (log-space for accuracy)
713	        exceeds_upper: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics > log_threshold_upper
714	        below_lower: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics < log_threshold_lower
715	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high"] = exceeds_upper.float().mean().item()
716	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low"] = below_lower.float().mean().item()
717	
718	    else:  # token-level
719	        # Token-level aggregation: the applied weights drive loss, std, and ESS,
720	        # while high/low fractions are measured from the raw pre-processing weights.
721	        metrics["rollout_is_mean"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()
722	
723	        # Fraction of tokens exceeding thresholds
724	        rollout_is_above_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights > rollout_is_threshold
725	        rollout_is_below_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower
726	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high"] = verl_F.masked_mean(
727	            rollout_is_above_threshold.float(), response_mask
728	        ).item()
729	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low"] = verl_F.masked_mean(
730	            rollout_is_below_threshold.float(), response_mask
731	        ).item()
732	
733	        # Max/min (mask out padding tokens)
734	        mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()
735	        metrics["rollout_is_max"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("-inf")).max().item()
736	        metrics["rollout_is_min"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("inf")).min().item()
737	
738	    # Compute standard deviation / ESS from the actual applied weights so exact
739	    # IcePop diagnostics preserve zeroed-out coefficients.
740	    mask_count: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum()
741	    if mask_count > 1:
742	        weights_for_std: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)
743	        mean_clamped: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std, response_mask)
744	        rollout_is_var: torch.Tensor = (
745	            verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std.square(), response_mask) - mean_clamped.square()
746	        )
747	        metrics["rollout_is_std"] = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(rollout_is_var, min=0.0)).item()
748	    else:
749	        metrics["rollout_is_std"] = 0.0
750	
751	    # Compute Effective Sample Size (ESS) for truncated weights
752	    weights_for_ess: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)
753	    mean_for_ess: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_ess, response_mask)
754	    is_weights_normalized: torch.Tensor = weights_for_ess / (mean_for_ess + 1e-8)  # Avoid division by zero
755	    metrics["rollout_is_eff_sample_size"] = (
756	        1.0 / verl_F.masked_mean(is_weights_normalized.square(), response_mask).item()
757	    )
758	
759	    # Add sequence-level metrics if weights have batch dimension
760	    if rollout_is_weights.dim() > 1:
761	        seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)
762	
763	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_mean"] = seq_mean_weights.mean().item()
764	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_std"] = seq_mean_weights.std().item() if seq_mean_weights.numel() > 1 else 0.0
765	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_max"] = seq_mean_weights.max().item()
766	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_min"] = seq_mean_weights.min().item()
767	
768	        # Sequence deviation from ideal weight (1.0)
769	        seq_deviation: torch.Tensor = (seq_mean_weights - 1.0).abs()
770	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_max_deviation"] = seq_deviation.max().item()
771	
772	        # Fraction of sequences with extreme weights. Use the raw (pre-truncation)
773	        # per-sequence mean: every clamped weight is <= rollout_is_threshold, so a mean
774	        # of clamped weights can never exceed it and the high fraction would be dead.
775	        raw_seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(raw_rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)
776	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_fraction_high"] = (raw_seq_mean_weights > rollout_is_threshold).float().mean().item()
777	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_fraction_low"] = (
778	            (raw_seq_mean_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower).float().mean().item()
779	        )
780	
781	    return metrics
782

784	def compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(
785	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
786	    rollout_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
787	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
788	    rollout_is: Optional[str] = None,
789	    rollout_is_threshold: Optional[str | float] = 2.0,
790	    rollout_is_batch_normalize: bool = False,
791	    rollout_rs: Optional[str] = None,
792	    rollout_rs_threshold: Optional[str | float] = None,
793	) -> tuple[Optional[DataProto], torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
794	    """Unified interface for computing IS weights and rejection masks.
795	
796	    This function combines IS weight calculation (truncated) and rejection sampling (masked)
797	    into a single pipeline.
798	
799	    Key design:
800	    - Separation of IS weights (for variance reduction) and rejection masks (for sample filtering)
801	    - Comprehensive metrics tracking for mismatch diagnosis
802	
803	    Args:
804	        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from the training policy (e.g., FSDP FP32),
805	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
806	        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from the rollout policy (e.g., vLLM BF16),
807	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
808	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
809	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
810	        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level (see compute_rollout_correction_weights for options).
811	            Set to None to disable IS weight computation.
812	        rollout_is_threshold: Threshold specification for IS weights.
813	            Single float implies TIS; "lower_upper" implies IcePop.
814	        rollout_rs: Rejection sampling aggregation modes as a comma separated string
815	            (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for the full list). Set to None to disable

902	def compute_offpolicy_metrics(
903	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
904	    rollout_log_prob: Optional[torch.Tensor],
905	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
906	) -> dict[str, Any]:
907	    """Compute off-policy diagnostic metrics (helper function).
908	
909	    This helper function operates on raw tensors and is used internally by:
910	    - compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask() in this module (automatically included)
911	    - Tests (test_rollout_corr.py, test_rollout_corr_integration.py)
912	
913	    These metrics help diagnose the off-policy gap between rollout and training policies,
914	    which can arise from:
915	    - Policy mismatch (e.g., vLLM BF16 vs FSDP FP32)
916	    - Model staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)
917	    - General distribution shifts
918	
919	    Key metrics:
920	    - kl: Direct KL divergence estimator KL(π_rollout || π_training)
921	    - k3_kl: K3 KL estimator for stability (more stable for small KL)
922	    - training_ppl: Perplexity of training policy
923	    - rollout_ppl: Perplexity of rollout policy
924	    - log_ppl_diff: Difference in log perplexities
925	    - ppl_ratio: Ratio of training PPL to rollout PPL
926	    - chi2_token: Token-level χ² divergence E[ρ²] - 1
927	    - chi2_seq: Sequence-level χ² divergence E[(∏ρ_t)²] - 1
928	
929	    Args:
930	        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from training policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)
931	        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from rollout policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)
932	        response_mask: Mask for valid tokens, shape (batch_size, seq_length)
933	
934	    Returns:
935	        Dictionary of off-policy metrics (without prefix)
936	    """
937	    # Validate that we have at least one valid token
938	    assert response_mask.any(), "Expected at least one valid token in response_mask"
939	
940	    metrics = {}
941	
942	    # 1. Training policy perplexity (always available)
943	    # Formula: exp(-1/|T| * Σ log π_training(y_t|y_<t))
944	    # where |T| is the number of tokens generated by the model
945	    mean_log_prob_training = verl_F.masked_mean(old_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)
946	    training_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_training).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL
947	    metrics["training_ppl"] = training_ppl.detach().item()
948	
949	    # Also log log-ppl for easier analysis (avoids exponential scale)
950	    metrics["training_log_ppl"] = (-mean_log_prob_training).mean().detach().item()
951	
952	    # 2. Compute rollout off-policy metrics (only if rollout_log_probs available)
953	    if rollout_log_prob is not None:
954	        # 2a. kl: Direct estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)
955	        # This is the standard KL divergence: E[log(π_rollout) - log(π_training)]
956	        # Positive value means rollout policy is more confident than training policy
957	        metrics["kl"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob - old_log_prob, response_mask).detach().item()
958	
959	        # 2b. k3_kl: K3 estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)
960	        # More stable for small KL values using: E[exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1]
961	        # Formula: KL ≈ E[r - log(r) - 1] where r = π_training/π_rollout
962	        log_ratio = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob
963	        k3_kl_matrix = torch.exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1
964	        metrics["k3_kl"] = verl_F.masked_mean(k3_kl_matrix, response_mask).detach().item()
965	
966	        # 2c. Rollout policy perplexity
967	        mean_log_prob_rollout = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)
968	        rollout_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL
969	        metrics["rollout_ppl"] = rollout_ppl.detach().item()
970	        metrics["rollout_log_ppl"] = (-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean().detach().item()
971	
972	        # 2d. Log PPL difference (sequence-level perplexity difference)
973	        # log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training
974	        # Since ppl = exp(-log_prob), we have:
975	        #   log(ppl_ratio) = log(training_ppl/rollout_ppl) = log_ppl_diff
976	        # Positive value means training assigns lower probability (higher PPL) than rollout
977	        log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training
978	        metrics["log_ppl_diff"] = log_ppl_diff.mean().detach().item()
979	        metrics["log_ppl_abs_diff"] = log_ppl_diff.abs().mean().detach().item()
980	        metrics["log_ppl_diff_max"] = log_ppl_diff.max().detach().item()
981	        metrics["log_ppl_diff_min"] = log_ppl_diff.min().detach().item()
982	
983	        # 2e. PPL ratio (how much higher is training PPL vs rollout PPL)
984	        # Compute per-sequence ratio first, then average
985	        # For numerical stability, compute in log space using log_ppl_diff
986	        # Note: log_ppl_diff = log(ppl_ratio), so ppl_ratio = exp(log_ppl_diff)
987	        # This is the inverse of geometric IS: ppl_ratio_i = 1 / geometric_is_i for each sequence
988	        ppl_ratio = torch.exp(log_ppl_diff).mean()  # mean(exp(log_ppl_diff)) = mean(ppl_ratio_i)
989	        metrics["ppl_ratio"] = ppl_ratio.detach().item()
990	
991	        # 2f. Chi-squared divergence: χ²(π_training || π_rollout) = E_μ[ρ²] - 1
992	        # where ρ = π_training / π_rollout and μ = π_rollout (rollout distribution)
993	        # This measures the variance of importance sampling weights
994	        # Token-level: E_token[ρ²] - 1 (averaged over all tokens)
995	        log_ratio_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
996	        rho_token = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe)  # ρ = π_training / π_rollout (token-level)
997	        rho_squared_token = rho_token.square()
998	        chi2_token = verl_F.masked_mean(rho_squared_token, response_mask) - 1.0
999	        metrics["chi2_token"] = chi2_token.detach().item()
1000	
1001	        # Sequence-level: E_seq[(Π ρ_t)²] - 1 = E_seq[exp(2 * Σ log ρ_t)] - 1
1002	        log_ratio_sum = verl_F.masked_sum(log_ratio, response_mask, axis=-1)  # Σ log ρ_t per sequence
1003	        log_ratio_sum_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio_sum, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
1004	        rho_squared_seq = torch.exp(2.0 * log_ratio_sum_safe)  # (Π ρ_t)²
1005	        chi2_seq = rho_squared_seq.mean() - 1.0
1006	        metrics["chi2_seq"] = chi2_seq.detach().item()
1007	
1008	    return metrics

Default lower threshold (reciprocal of upper threshold)\n    rollout_is_threshold_lower = (\n        1.0 / rollout_is_threshold if rollout_is_threshold_lower is None else rollout_is_threshold_lower\n    )\n\n    # Precompute log thresholds for accurate checks\n    log_threshold_upper: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold, device=device))\n    log_threshold_lower: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold_lower, device=device))\n\n    # Compute metrics based on aggregation level\n    if rollout_is == \"sequence\":\n        # Sequence-level aggregation: use log-space for unclamped stats\n        log_max: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.max()\n        log_min: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.min()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_max\"] = torch.exp(torch.clamp(log_max, max=SAFETY_BOUND)).item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_min\"] = torch.exp(log_min).item()\n\n        # Mean uses truncated weights to avoid overflow\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_mean\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()\n\n        # Fraction of weights exceeding thresholds (log-space for accuracy)\n        exceeds_upper: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics > log_threshold_upper\n        below_lower: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics < log_threshold_lower\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high\"] = exceeds_upper.float().mean().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low\"] = below_lower.float().mean().item()\n\n    else:  # token-level\n        # Token-level aggregation: the applied weights drive loss, std, and ESS,\n        # while high/low fractions are measured from the raw pre-processing weights.\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_mean\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()\n\n        # Fraction of tokens exceeding thresholds\n        rollout_is_above_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights > rollout_is_threshold\n        rollout_is_below_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(\n            rollout_is_above_threshold.float(), response_mask\n        ).item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(\n            rollout_is_below_threshold.float(), response_mask\n        ).item()\n\n        # Max/min (mask out padding tokens)\n        mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_max\"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float(\"-inf\")).max().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_min\"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float(\"inf\")).min().item()\n\n    # Compute standard deviation / ESS from the actual applied weights so exact\n    # IcePop diagnostics preserve zeroed-out coefficients.\n    mask_count: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum()\n    if mask_count > 1:\n        weights_for_std: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)\n        mean_clamped: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std, response_mask)\n        rollout_is_var: torch.Tensor = (\n            verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std.square(), response_mask) - mean_clamped.square()\n        )\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_std\"] = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(rollout_is_var, min=0.0)).item()\n    else:\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_std\"] = 0.0\n\n    # Compute Effective Sample Size (ESS) for truncated weights\n    weights_for_ess: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)\n    mean_for_ess: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_ess, response_mask)\n    is_weights_normalized: torch.Tensor = weights_for_ess / (mean_for_ess + 1e-8)  # Avoid division by zero\n    metrics[\"rollout_is_eff_sample_size\"] = (\n        1.0 / verl_F.masked_mean(is_weights_normalized.square(), response_mask).item()\n    )\n\n    # Add sequence-level metrics if weights have batch dimension\n    if rollout_is_weights.dim() > 1:\n        seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)\n\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_mean\"] = seq_mean_weights.mean().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_std\"] = seq_mean_weights.std().item() if seq_mean_weights.numel() > 1 else 0.0\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_max\"] = seq_mean_weights.max().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_min\"] = seq_mean_weights.min().item()\n\n        # Sequence deviation from ideal weight (1.0)\n        seq_deviation: torch.Tensor = (seq_mean_weights - 1.0).abs()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_max_deviation\"] = seq_deviation.max().item()\n\n        # Fraction of sequences with extreme weights. Use the raw (pre-truncation)\n        # per-sequence mean: every clamped weight is <= rollout_is_threshold, so a mean\n        # of clamped weights can never exceed it and the high fraction would be dead.\n        raw_seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(raw_rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_fraction_high\"] = (raw_seq_mean_weights > rollout_is_threshold).float().mean().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_fraction_low\"] = (\n            (raw_seq_mean_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower).float().mean().item()\n        )\n\n    return metrics\n\n\ndef compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(\n    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    response_mask: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_is: Optional[str] = None,\n    rollout_is_threshold: Optional[str | float] = 2.0,\n    rollout_is_batch_normalize: bool = False,\n    rollout_rs: Optional[str] = None,\n    rollout_rs_threshold: Optional[str | float] = None,\n) -> tuple[Optional[DataProto], torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Unified interface for computing IS weights and rejection masks.\n\n    This function combines IS weight calculation (truncated) and rejection sampling (masked)\n    into a single pipeline.\n\n    Key design:\n    - Separation of IS weights (for variance reduction) and rejection masks (for sample filtering)\n    - Comprehensive metrics tracking for mismatch diagnosis\n\n    Args:\n        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from the training policy (e.g., FSDP FP32),\n            shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from the rollout policy (e.g., vLLM BF16),\n            shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),\n            shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level (see compute_rollout_correction_weights for options).\n            Set to None to disable IS weight computation.\n        rollout_is_threshold: Threshold specification for IS weights.\n            Single float implies TIS; \"lower_upper\" implies IcePop.\n        rollout_rs: Rejection sampling aggregation modes as a comma separated string\n            (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for the full list). Set to None to disable\n            rejection sampling.\n        rollout_rs_threshold: Threshold specification string (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for details).\n            Provide one threshold per option (comma separated). For K1-style options, specify\n            ``lower_upper`` to denote the lower/upper ratio bounds.\n        rollout_is_batch_normalize: Whether to normalize IS weights to have mean=1.0 per batch.\n            Default: False.\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple containing:\n            rollout_is_weights_proto: DataProto with IS weights (None if rollout_is is None),\n                key \"rollout_is_weights\", shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n            modified_response_mask: Response mask with rejection sampling applied,\n                shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n            metrics: Dictionary of all metrics (prefixed with \"rollout_corr/\"), including:\n                - IS weight statistics\n                - Rejection sampling rates\n                - Policy mismatch metrics (KL, PPL, etc.)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Validate input masks\n    if not response_mask.any():\n        raise ValueError(\"response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).\")\n    if old_log_prob.shape != rollout_log_prob.shape:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"old_log_prob shape {old_log_prob.shape} does not match rollout_log_prob shape {rollout_log_prob.shape}.\"\n        )\n    if old_log_prob.shape != response_mask.shape:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"log_prob shape {old_log_prob.shape} does not match response_mask shape {response_mask.shape}.\"\n        )\n\n    # Step 1: Compute log ratio (log(π_train / π_rollout))\n    log_ratio: torch.Tensor = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob\n    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}\n\n    # Step 2: Compute IS weights (if enabled)\n    rollout_is_weights: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None\n    if rollout_is is not None and rollout_is_threshold is not None:\n        rollout_is_weights, is_metrics = compute_rollout_correction_weights(\n            log_ratio=log_ratio,\n            response_mask=response_mask,\n            rollout_is=rollout_is,\n            rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold,\n            rollout_is_batch_normalize=rollout_is_batch_normalize,\n        )\n        metrics.update(is_metrics)\n\n    # Step 3: Compute rejection mask (if enabled)\n    modified_response_mask: torch.Tensor = response_mask.clone()\n    if rollout_rs is not None:\n        if rollout_rs_threshold is None:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"rollout_rs_threshold must be explicitly provided when rollout_rs is enabled. \"\n                \"Set rollout_rs_threshold to the desired threshold value.\"\n            )\n        modified_response_mask, rs_metrics = compute_rollout_rejection_mask(\n            log_ratio=log_ratio,\n            response_mask=response_mask,\n            rollout_rs=rollout_rs,\n            rollout_rs_threshold=rollout_rs_threshold,\n        )\n        metrics.update(rs_metrics)\n\n    # Step 4: Compute off-policy metrics (KL, PPL, χ², etc.)\n    offpolicy_metrics: dict[str, float] = compute_offpolicy_metrics(\n        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,\n        rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,\n        response_mask=response_mask,\n    )\n    metrics.update(offpolicy_metrics)\n\n    # Step 6: Add \"rollout_corr/\" prefix to all metrics for logging consistency\n    metrics_scalar: dict[str, float] = {}\n    for key, value in metrics.items():\n        if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):\n            metrics_scalar[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value.item()\n        else:\n            metrics_scalar[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value\n\n    # Step 7: Wrap IS weights in DataProto for consistency with API\n    rollout_is_weights_proto: Optional[DataProto] = None\n    if rollout_is_weights is not None:\n        rollout_is_weights_proto = DataProto.from_dict(tensors={\"rollout_is_weights\": rollout_is_weights})\n\n    return rollout_is_weights_proto, modified_response_mask, metrics_scalar\n\n\ndef compute_offpolicy_metrics(\n    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_log_prob: Optional[torch.Tensor],\n    response_mask: torch.Tensor,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Compute off-policy diagnostic metrics (helper function).\n\n    This helper function operates on raw tensors and is used internally by:\n    - compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask() in this module (automatically included)\n    - Tests (test_rollout_corr.py, test_rollout_corr_integration.py)\n\n    These metrics help diagnose the off-policy gap between rollout and training policies,\n    which can arise from:\n    - Policy mismatch (e.g., vLLM BF16 vs FSDP FP32)\n    - Model staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)\n    - General distribution shifts\n\n    Key metrics:\n    - kl: Direct KL divergence estimator KL(π_rollout || π_training)\n    - k3_kl: K3 KL estimator for stability (more stable for small KL)\n    - training_ppl: Perplexity of training policy\n    - rollout_ppl: Perplexity of rollout policy\n    - log_ppl_diff: Difference in log perplexities\n    - ppl_ratio: Ratio of training PPL to rollout PPL\n    - chi2_token: Token-level χ² divergence E[ρ²] - 1\n    - chi2_seq: Sequence-level χ² divergence E[(∏ρ_t)²] - 1\n\n    Args:\n        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from training policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from rollout policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        response_mask: Mask for valid tokens, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary of off-policy metrics (without prefix)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Validate that we have at least one valid token\n    assert response_mask.any(), \"Expected at least one valid token in response_mask\"\n\n    metrics = {}\n\n    # 1. Training policy perplexity (always available)\n    # Formula: exp(-1/|T| * Σ log π_training(y_t|y_<t))\n    # where |T| is the number of tokens generated by the model\n    mean_log_prob_training = verl_F.masked_mean(old_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)\n    training_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_training).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL\n    metrics[\"training_ppl\"] = training_ppl.detach().item()\n\n    # Also log log-ppl for easier analysis (avoids exponential scale)\n    metrics[\"training_log_ppl\"] = (-mean_log_prob_training).mean().detach().item()\n\n    # 2. Compute rollout off-policy metrics (only if rollout_log_probs available)\n    if rollout_log_prob is not None:\n        # 2a. kl: Direct estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)\n        # This is the standard KL divergence: E[log(π_rollout) - log(π_training)]\n        # Positive value means rollout policy is more confident than training policy\n        metrics[\"kl\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob - old_log_prob, response_mask).detach().item()\n\n        # 2b. k3_kl: K3 estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)\n        # More stable for small KL values using: E[exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1]\n        # Formula: KL ≈ E[r - log(r) - 1] where r = π_training/π_rollout\n        log_ratio = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob\n        k3_kl_matrix = torch.exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1\n        metrics[\"k3_kl\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(k3_kl_matrix, response_mask).detach().item()\n\n        # 2c. Rollout policy perplexity\n        mean_log_prob_rollout = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)\n        rollout_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL\n        metrics[\"rollout_ppl\"] = rollout_ppl.detach().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_log_ppl\"] = (-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean().detach().item()\n\n        # 2d. Log PPL difference (sequence-level perplexity difference)\n        # log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training\n        # Since ppl = exp(-log_prob), we have:\n        #   log(ppl_ratio) = log(training_ppl/rollout_ppl) = log_ppl_diff\n        # Positive value means training assigns lower probability (higher PPL) than rollout\n        log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_diff\"] = log_ppl_diff.mean().detach().item()\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_abs_diff\"] = log_ppl_diff.abs().mean().detach().item()\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_diff_max\"] = log_ppl_diff.max().detach().item()\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_diff_min\"] = log_ppl_diff.min().detach().item()\n\n        # 2e. PPL ratio (how much higher is training PPL vs rollout PPL)\n        # Compute per-sequence ratio first, then average\n        # For numerical stability, compute in log space using log_ppl_diff\n        # Note: log_ppl_diff = log(ppl_ratio), so ppl_ratio = exp(log_ppl_diff)\n        # This is the inverse of geometric IS: ppl_ratio_i = 1 / geometric_is_i for each sequence\n        ppl_ratio = torch.exp(log_ppl_diff).mean()  # mean(exp(log_ppl_diff)) = mean(ppl_ratio_i)\n        metrics[\"ppl_ratio\"] = ppl_ratio.detach().item()\n\n        # 2f. Chi-squared divergence: χ²(π_training || π_rollout) = E_μ[ρ²] - 1\n        # where ρ = π_training / π_rollout and μ = π_rollout (rollout distribution)\n        # This measures the variance of importance sampling weights\n        # Token-level: E_token[ρ²] - 1 (averaged over all tokens)\n        log_ratio_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)\n        rho_token = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe)  # ρ = π_training / π_rollout (token-level)\n        rho_squared_token = rho_token.square()\n        chi2_token = verl_F.masked_mean(rho_squared_token, response_mask) - 1.0\n        metrics[\"chi2_token\"] = chi2_token.detach().item()\n\n        # Sequence-level: E_seq[(Π ρ_t)²] - 1 = E_seq[exp(2 * Σ log ρ_t)] - 1\n        log_ratio_sum = verl_F.masked_sum(log_ratio, response_mask, axis=-1)  # Σ log ρ_t per sequence\n        log_ratio_sum_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio_sum, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)\n        rho_squared_seq = torch.exp(2.0 * log_ratio_sum_safe)  # (Π ρ_t)²\n        chi2_seq = rho_squared_seq.mean() - 1.0\n        metrics[\"chi2_seq\"] = chi2_seq.detach().item()\n\n    return metrics\n\n\ndef compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch(\n    batch: DataProto, rollout_corr_config: RolloutCorrectionConfig\n) -> tuple[DataProto, dict]:\n    \"\"\"Compute rollout correction weights and apply rejection sampling.\n\n    Computes importance sampling weights to correct for off-policy issues between\n    rollout and training policies. Applies rejection sampling by modifying response_mask.\n    Always updates response_mask; conditionally adds IS weights.\n\n    Key behavior:\n    - response_mask: ALWAYS updated with rejection (RS exclusions removed from training)\n    - rollout_is_weights: Added to batch ONLY if rollout_is parameter is set\n\n    This separation ensures:\n    - Rejection works independently of IS weight application\n    - Metrics can be monitored before enabling IS weight correction\n\n    Args:\n        batch: DataProto with old_log_probs, rollout_log_probs, response_mask\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple of (updated_batch, metrics):\n            updated_batch: Batch with modified response_mask (always) and rollout_is_weights (if enabled)\n            metrics: Dict of IS and off-policy metrics, all with \"rollout_corr/\" prefix\n\n    Note:\n        The implementation is copied from szrlee <szrlee@gmail.com>.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get new API parameters directly from config\n    rollout_is = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_is\", None)\n    rollout_is_threshold = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_is_threshold\", 2.0)\n    rollout_is_batch_normalize = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_is_batch_normalize\", False)\n    rollout_rs = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_rs\", None)\n    rollout_rs_threshold = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_rs_threshold\", None)\n\n    # Compute IS weights and get modified response_mask\n    rollout_is_weights, modified_response_mask, rollout_corr_metrics = compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(\n        old_log_prob=batch.batch[\"old_log_probs\"],\n        rollout_log_prob=batch.batch[\"rollout_log_probs\"],\n        response_mask=batch.batch[\"response_mask\"],\n        rollout_is=rollout_is,\n        rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold,\n        rollout_is_batch_normalize=rollout_is_batch_normalize,\n        rollout_rs=rollout_rs,\n        rollout_rs_threshold=rollout_rs_threshold,\n    )\n\n    # ALWAYS update response_mask with rejection applied\n    batch.batch[\"response_mask\"] = modified_response_mask\n\n    # Add IS weights to batch if computed\n    if rollout_is_weights is not None:\n        batch = batch.union(rollout_is_weights)\n\n    return batch, rollout_corr_metrics\n\n\ndef compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs(\n    log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    response_mask: torch.Tensor,\n) -> dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Compute rollout correction metrics from log probabilities during training.\n\n    This function is used in the actor to compute metrics using the CURRENT policy\n    log probabilities versus rollout log probabilities, allowing tracking of the\n    off-policy gap as training progresses.\n\n    It computes off-policy diagnostic metrics (KL, PPL, χ²) from log probabilities.\n\n    Args:\n        log_prob: Current policy log probabilities, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        rollout_log_prob: Rollout policy log probabilities, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        response_mask: Valid token mask, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary of metrics with \"rollout_corr/\" prefix\n    \"\"\"\n    # Compute off-policy diagnostic metrics\n    offpolicy_metrics = compute_offpolicy_metrics(\n        old_log_prob=log_prob,\n        rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,\n        response_mask=response_mask,\n    )\n\n    # Add rollout_corr/ prefix to all metrics\n    metrics_with_prefix = {}\n    for key, value in offpolicy_metrics.items():\n        if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):\n            metrics_with_prefix[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value.item()\n        else:\n            metrics_with_prefix[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value\n\n    return metrics_with_prefix\n\n\ndef apply_bypass_mode(\n    batch: DataProto,\n    rollout_corr_config: Optional[RolloutCorrectionConfig] = None,\n    policy_loss_config: PolicyLossConfig = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    Setup bypass mode: Use rollout_log_probs as old_log_probs.\n\n    Bypass mode skips expensive actor forward pass for old_log_prob computation\n    by setting old_log_probs = rollout_log_probs (2 policies instead of 3).\n\n    Uses compute_policy_loss_bypass_mode() which supports:\n    - loss_type=\"ppo_clip\" (default): PPO clipped objective (IS handled by ratio)\n    - loss_type=\"reinforce\": REINFORCE with explicit IS weights\n\n    Both loss types benefit from rejection sampling (RS) which masks out-of-distribution samples.\n\n    Note:\n        The implementation is copied from szrlee <szrlee@gmail.com>.\n    \"\"\"\n    from omegaconf import open_dict\n\n    if \"rollout_log_probs\" not in batch.batch:\n        raise ValueError(\n            \"bypass_mode=True requires rollout_log_probs in batch. \"\n            \"Ensure rollout worker is configured to calculate_log_probs=true.\"\n        )\n\n    # Use rollout log probs as old log probs (zero-cost substitution)\n    batch.batch[\"old_log_probs\"] = batch.batch[\"rollout_log_probs\"]\n\n    with open_dict(policy_loss_config):\n        # Pass rollout_correction config to actor for loss computation and metrics\n        policy_loss_config[\"rollout_correction\"] = rollout_corr_config\n        # Always use bypass_mode loss function which handles both loss_types\n        policy_loss_config[\"loss_mode\"] = \"bypass_mode\"\n", "numLines": 1143, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 1143}}
